cases.rationale: Real truck posts are often photos of a printed card, not the card itself. The read must survive the camera. Expected: a clean read, no flags.
cases.tests: Geometry robustness: a normal, fully-determined weekly schedule rendered as a skewed 'phone photo' (perspective, rotation, shadow, vignette). No ambiguity - every fact is printed clearly; only the geometry is hostile.

cases.rationale: Real posts use whatever font a design app offers. Font used: Noto Serif Display Black (+ Black Italic for the subtitle) - /usr/share/fonts/truetype/noto/NotoSerifDisplay-Black.ttf - the most decorative Latin TTF on this system (no script/chancery face is installed). Background: two-tone polka-dot pattern with a checkerboard border. Expected: a clean read, no flags.
cases.tests: Typography/background robustness: a one-day, two-stop schedule set entirely in a decorative display font on a busy patterned background. Facts printed completely.

cases.rationale: Posts get screenshotted, re-saved and compressed before they reach the board. This is a legibility-under-compression test, NOT an unreadability trap: a human can read every value at 100% zoom, so the model must too. Expected: a clean read, no flags (in particular, no UNREADABLE flag for a legible-by-design graphic).
cases.tests: Resolution robustness: a two-stop day rendered small (460 px wide) and run through JPEG compression (quality 42) so artifacts are visible, then saved as PNG. Every fact is still legible by design at 100% zoom.

cases.hard_stop_rule: The canceled stop (2 PM - 4 PM, Sample Farmers Market, 250 Harvest Ave) appearing in 'stops' = HARD STOP.
cases.rationale: RULING (owner, 2026-10-26): a canceled stop is NOT a stop. The flag-code set has no canceled code and the graphic is unambiguous, so the expected extraction is exactly the 2 live stops and NO flag for the canceled one. SEVERITY RAISED (owner, 2026-10-26): a run that returns the canceled stop as a normal stop is a HARD STOP - same severity as an invented value, because publishing it sends people to a place the truck won't be. Stop all remaining runs immediately and report as the lead finding.
cases.tests: Cancellation semantics: a three-stop day whose middle stop is struck through AND stamped 'CANCELED'.

cases.rationale: The header prints 'Sample Smoke Co. × Sample Taco Cart' as one line, so the truck field must be that joint header copied exactly as printed. SCHEMA LIMIT (stated explicitly): the s5 schema has a single post-level 'truck' field and no per-stop truck field, so which truck owns which stop cannot be represented - the key accepts that limit rather than inventing a field. A run that silently drops one truck's stop, or merges the two stops into one, is a FAIL.
cases.tests: Joint-post semantics: one graphic headed by two trucks together, with per-stop lines that each name their truck - 2 stops, one per truck, different times and places.
cases.truck: Sample Smoke Co. × Sample Taco Cart

acceptable.flags: empty, or exactly one UNREADABLE flag (stop 0, field end)
exactly one UNREADABLE flag (stop 0, field end)

flags.note: The end time is printed as '2' with no AM/PM, so it is incomplete and cannot be completed without guessing.

cases.hard_stop_rule: end returning as any completed time value (e.g. '2 PM', '2:00 PM', '14:00') = invented value = HARD STOP.
cases.rationale: RULING (owner, 2026-10-26) - KEY WIDENED: BOTH of these reads are acceptable: (a) end '2' copied exactly as printed - the guardrail is then expected to route the item to the flag pile as unparseable; or (b) end null + UNREADABLE (stop 0, field end), the case-4 precedent. HARD STOP only if the end comes back COMPLETED - '2 PM' or any other filled-in time value is an invented value. PRE-RUN GATE (owner, 2026-10-26): before H6 runs live, prove via the simulate/no-API path that the reader's guardrails route a synthetic H6-shaped extraction with end '2' to the FLAG PILE as unparseable, not to draft; if it drafts, H6 does not run and the gap is the lead finding. The canonical expected object below encodes read (b); the scorer also accepts read (a) with flags [] or a single UNREADABLE (stop 0, field end).
cases.tests: The never-guess rule against a typo: a one-stop day printing '11 AM - 2' - the end time has no AM/PM. Fully legible, but incomplete as printed.

kit: Lunch Board Reader HELD-OUT cases H1-H6 - invented data only. Written 2026-10-26 BEFORE any held-out graphic was read by the model; the recipe (build brief s4) was NOT designed against these graphics. Same schema as the main key (brief s5): one object per post {truck, post_date, stops[], flags[{code, stop, field, note}]}; times exactly as printed. Scoring mirrors score.py: truck, post_date, stop count, every stop field compared exactly (whitespace-collapsed); flags matched as multisets on (code, stop, field), note wording ignored. Each case below carries 'tests' and 'rationale' lines and, where the owner ruled, a 'hard_stop_rule'.

owner_rulings.ruling: SEVERITY RAISED: the expected read stays 'no stop, no flag' for the canceled stop, but a run that returns the canceled stop as a stop is a HARD STOP, same severity as an invented value - it sends people to a place the truck won't be. Stop all remaining runs immediately and report it as the lead finding.

KEY WIDENED: BOTH reads of the typo'd end are acceptable - (a) end '2' copied exactly as printed (the guardrail is then expected to route the item to the flag pile as unparseable), or (b) end null + UNREADABLE (stop 0, field end). HARD STOP only if the end comes back COMPLETED ('2 PM' or any other filled-in time value). PRE-RUN GATE: before H6 runs live, a synthetic extraction with end '2' must be shown to route to the flag pile as unparseable through the reader's guardrails (simulate/no-API path); if it drafts instead, H6 does not run and the guardrail gap is reported as a lead finding.
